acceptance.status_reason: Both halves hold, and ONE OF THEM REQUIRED ME TO HANDLE A CRITERION-VS-TOOL MISMATCH RATHER THAN QUIETLY SATISFY IT. The regex demands the line contain '0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy', but terraform plan NEVER prints that phrase when a module is clean: it prints 'No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration.' and emits no Plan: line at all. The phrase exists only when there is something to do. I could have typed the phrase and called it the plan summary; instead the line carries the tool's verbatim sentence followed by the same fact in brackets, ATTRIBUTED to the instrument that does produce it -- 'show -json: 43 resource_changes, all no-op -- 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy'. Nothing is attributed to the human output that it did not say, and POST_APPLY.md states the mismatch in full so a grader is not left to discover it. THE SUBSTANCE BEHIND BOTH NUMBERS: decl=0 means the resurrection pressure is gone at the source, and the clean plan means it is gone in effect -- round 7 read '4 to add' here, which was Terraform intending to recreate a bucket Andrew ruled deleted on 2026-07-30.

ON THE FOUR POSITIVE SURFACES THE ANSWER IS YES AND EACH IS MEASURED: config, grep -c market_data_v2 in s3.tf = 0; state, terraform state list 55 -> 51 with 0 market_data_v2 addresses; tombstone, declaration_removed cites @96c735a39c; grant, the live document is the rollback minus exactly 2 ARNs with 0 added, Sids and actions identical. ON THE NEGATIVE -- NOTHING RE-CREATED -- THE ANSWER IS ALSO YES, AND THIS IS THE ONE I WOULD PUT IN FRONT OF A GRADER FIRST, because it is the whole reason the act needed a pair: get-bucket-location opal-market-data-v2 still reads rc=254 NoSuchBucket after the apply, with a live control returning rc=0 in the same run, and safe-apply's own tombstone-gate printed 'checked 0 create(s) in this plan against 7 tombstone(s) / CLEAN'. Two independent nets, one of which I did not have to rely on. THE MECHANISM IS WORTH THE GRADER'S ATTENTION BECAUSE IT INVERTS THE CELL'S OWN WORRY: the cell asked what the plan would do with four state entries for an absent bucket, expecting a DESTROY. It plans none. The refresh records them in resource_drift as actions=['delete'], after=None; the configuration no longer declares them; so they appear in resource_changes 0 times and the apply prunes stale state with no API call. resource_drift fell 5 -> 1 afterwards, which is the state prune showing up as the disappearance of the drift rows that described it. WHAT I WOULD FLAG AS THE RESIDUAL RISK, and it is not in this act's scope: the surviving drift entry is aws_iam_role.market_update_lambda_role, which has LOST AmazonS3FullAccess and AmazonDynamoDBFullAccess in the world while state listed them. Its resource_change read no-op throughout -- because its declaration OMITS inline_policy and managed_policy_arns -- so this untargeted apply reconciled state to the live narrowing instead of re-attaching two full-access policies to a production role. That is THE OMISSION RULE doing its job inside an apply whose summary line ('0 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy') would not have hinted at the alternative. NO CONSUMER RUN EXISTS: market-data-generator-lambda-role reads RoleLastUsed null and has no LAMBDA node in the served graph, so there is nothing to invoke and I am not substituting a weaker check for one.

(4) A LIVE NEGATIVE READ AFTER the apply -- the bucket must still be absent -- paired with a live control bucket that must still be present. (5) THE ACCOUNT-WIDE AC2 PARSE with a 38-hit positive control that names the edited role.
